source_text: Amen dico tibi, priusquam gallus cantet, ter me negabis. Quaeritur utrum si deprecatus fuisset ut repelleretur praecognita denegatio, forsitan non denegasset — sicut Ninivitis exoratus quae per Jonam praedixerat non fecit. Gloria Christo. Amen.
thought_title: Could Peter's denial have been averted by prayer?
orientation: Origen is still discussing Peter's predicted denial, now asking whether Peter could have prayed to have the foreknown denial turned away, as Nineveh's repentance turned away Jonah's announced destruction.
pass_a_gloss: Truly I say to you, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times. It is asked whether, if he had prayed that the foreknown denial be driven away, perhaps he would not have denied — just as, having been entreated by the Ninevites, he did not do what he had foretold through Jonah. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: Keeps the passive participle force of praecognita as 'known beforehand,' matching Origen's concern with divine foreknowledge and human action.
Repello has a stronger force than 'removed'; it suggests actively pushing back or averting the foreknown event.
Exoratus is passive, emphasizing that God was moved by the Ninevites' plea; 'entreated' preserves the passive construction.
Keeps the simple verb facere with its object implied, matching the source's brevity and avoiding interpretive expansion.

bible_refs.note: Amen dico tibi, priusquam gallus cantet, ter me negabis
sicut Ninivitis exoratus quae per Jonam praedixerat non fecit

pass_b_english: "Truly I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times" (Matthew 26:34). The question is raised whether, if Peter had prayed that the foreknown denial be driven away, he might not have denied him after all—just as God, having been entreated by the Ninevites, did not do what he had foretold through Jonah (Jonah 3:10). Glory to Christ. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: The question is raised whether, if Peter had prayed
last_rejected.why: Passive 'quaeritur' hides Origen as the one raising this question; English makes it impersonal.
last_rejected.fix: I ask whether, if Peter had prayed that the foreknown denial be driven away, he might not have denied him after all.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Quaeritur' is impersonal passive; 'the question is raised' accurately renders it without hiding any named speaker.

last_rejected.quote: did not do what he had foretold
last_rejected.source_quote: quae per Jonam praedixerat non fecit
last_rejected.why: Latin 'quae' refers to the threatened destruction of Nineveh, not 'what' generally; 'the things' or 'it' needed.
last_rejected.fix: did not bring about the destruction he had foretold through Jonah.
last_rejected.ruling: 'What he had foretold' correctly renders 'quae praedixerat'; antecedent is clear from context. No meaning lost.
